description.value: The study examined emotional conflict adaptation and related neural activation and connectivity abnormalities in generalized anxiety disorder.

spans.text: In this study, we investigated emotional conflict adaptation using a paradigm in which emotional processing is regulated spontaneously and in the absence of explicit instruction.

description.value: Participants categorized facial affect while ignoring overlaid affect label words.

spans.text: subjects were asked to identify the expression of a face (fearful or happy) while ignoring an overlying emotion word (“fear” or “happy”), which either matches (congruent) or conflicts (incongruent) with the facial expression.

stimuli.value: happy or fearful facial expression photographs overlaid with the words “FEAR” or “HAPPY”

spans.text: The task consisted of 148 presentations of happy or fearful facial expression photographs drawn from the set of Ekman and Friesen ( 38 ), overlaid with the words “FEAR” or “HAPPY”.
Subjects indicated facial affect with a button press response.

instructions.value: Categorize the facial affect as fearful or happy while ignoring the overlaid affect label word, which was either congruent or incongruent with the facial expression; respond with a button press.
